text:
elaine_pm: Quick sketch for a new contract mode I'm calling "flex-lock" — hybrid reserved pool that lets customers carry a small % of unused burst forward and gives ops soft-shaping rules. Looking for dev + sales feedback before we turn into a spec.

sam_eng: curious — how is this different from carryover proposals we've seen?

elaine_pm: short answer: more explicit per-tenant shaping + controlled carryover budget. goal is to reduce surprise throttles for customers who slightly underuse committed burst, while keeping predictable capacity.

maria_infra: can you drop the basic mechanics? numbers help.

elaine_pm: sure. draft rules: 1) commit X tokens/month for pool; 2) reserve baseline headroom H; 3) up to C% of unused burst can be carried to next month (carry cap = min(C% * committed_burst, absolute_cap)); 4) carried burst usable only for short bursts and subject to soft-eviction if global pressure.

nate_sales: from GTM — customers asked for something like this. We need clear SLAs: what happens when we evict carried usage? charge? credits?

elaine_pm: proposal: carried credits are free until we preempt; if preempted, we throttle but don't bill extra. If customer exceeds both commit + carried, normal overage pricing applies.

zach_sre: soft-eviction concerns: how do we surface preemption to oncall and customers? ops needs telemetry and alerting.

sam_eng: implementation idea: add an admission token with metadata {mode: "flex-lock", carried_budget: N}. Router checks token, scores request against baseline first then carried pool; if global utilization > threshold, carried tokens become eligible for preemption, LIFO.

anya_research: also think about fairness for latency-sensitive tenants. Carried credits shouldn't kick in for low-latency routes (e.g., 99th p95 SLA tier) unless customer opts in.

maria_infra: ops knobs needed: 1) global carried_preempt_threshold (util%); 2) per-region carry limits; 3) preempt_grace_seconds for in-flight KV cache sessions.

elaine_pm: yep — draft config block in spec: 
```json
{
  "mode": "flex-lock",
  "commit_burst": 1000000,
  "carry_percent": 0.2,
  "absolute_carry_cap": 200000,
  "preempt_threshold": 0.92,
  "preempt_policy": "soft-lifo",
  "sla_exempt_routes": ["low-latency"]
}
```

sam_eng: rough effort estimate? router + billing + console UX + telemetry. I'd call it 4-6 sprints across infra/serving/billing.

nate_sales: we should prepare 2 pilot offers: (A) small flex-lock for startups (20% carry, no SLA change) and (B) enterprise flex-lock (custom carry, guaranteed minimal spill protection).

zach_sre: ops runbook asks: add an incident subflow when carried preemption rate > 3% for >= 5m — auto-alert to capacity oncall + product.

elaine_pm: action items: @sam_eng draft API + admission semantics, @maria_infra list infra knobs and telemetry metrics, @zach_sre draft runbook snippet, @nate_sales outline pilot packaging. I'll synthesize into a spec doc next week.

anya_research: QA note — include eval prompts for degraded-carry scenarios so we can detect quality regressions before GA.

maria_infra: question: rollback path? if flex-lock causes instability, can we toggle global flag off quickly?

sam_eng: yes, we should gate behind a runtime feature flag per-region + per-pool. quick kill switch at router level.

nate_sales: any blockers for putting this on the roadmap for Q3 pilot?

elaine_pm: main blockers: billing mapping clarity, legal ok on contract language, and infra telemetry. If those items are green by end of sprint, we pencil pilot.

zach_sre: noted. I'll add telemetry requirements to the ops backlog.

elaine_pm: thanks all. I pushed a tiny proto to the shared drive: https://redwood.internal/specs/flex-lock-proto — please add comments. :thumbsup:

sam_eng: will review tomorrow.

maria_infra: ack.

nate_sales: looping in legal early.

anya_research: adding eval ticket now.

zach_sre: closing loop on runbook later today.
